question: Who is at war with syria and why?
text:
As of **November 24, 2026**, **Israel is the main foreign country carrying out military operations in Syria**, but the two aren’t fighting a full-scale war. Inside Syria, the government still faces an **ISIS insurgency** and localized violence. These are separate conflicts. ([dppa.un.org](https://dppa.un.org/sites/default/files/2026-09/2026-09-17%20SECCO%20UN%20Deputy%20Special%20Envoy%20for%20Syria%20Briefing%20as%20Delivered%20-%20English.pdf?utm_source=openai))

- **Israel:** After Bashar al-Assad’s government fell on **December 8, 2024**, Israel moved troops into the UN-monitored buffer zone near the Golan Heights and carried out strikes and raids in Syria. Israel says it wants to keep hostile armed groups away from its border and that some operations are meant to protect Syria’s Druze minority. Syria says the operations violate its sovereignty, and the UN says Israel’s military presence and activity in the buffer zone violate the 1974 disengagement agreement. ([digitallibrary.un.org](https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4129331/files/A_81_354-EN.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **ISIS:** The Islamic State no longer holds the territory it once controlled, but its fighters still carry out attacks and seek to undermine the new Syrian government. This is an insurgency, not a war with another country. ([euaa.europa.eu](https://www.euaa.europa.eu/syria-security-situation/1-general-description-security-situation?utm_source=openai))
- **Other armed groups:** In the south, tensions persist between Damascus and local Druze factions over security and who governs the area. In the northeast, major fighting between the government and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces ended with a **January 2026** agreement, though tensions remain. ([dppa.un.org](https://dppa.un.org/sites/default/files/2026-09/2026-09-17%20SECCO%20UN%20Deputy%20Special%20Envoy%20for%20Syria%20Briefing%20as%20Delivered%20-%20English.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The **2011–2024 civil war** was a different conflict: it began after Assad’s government cracked down on anti-government protests and ended with his overthrow. The violence today is not simply that same war continuing. ([cfr.org](https://www.cfr.org/global-conflict-tracker/conflict/conflict-syria?utm_source=openai))
